text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age and the brief, spontaneous nature of the episode without positional triggers, have you noticed any slurred speech, double vision, or limb weakness? REQUEST TEST: Head_CTI

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous assessment of Gastroenteritis is inconsistent with the primary symptom of vertigo; vomiting in your case is likely secondary to the inner ear disturbance. Since you denied neurological deficits, let's confirm if the episode was strictly rotational and if you felt any nausea while lying down. Can you confirm if the spinning lasted less than a minute and if you felt any ear fullness or ringing at that time? REQUEST TEST: Audiometry; REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Internal_Auditory_Canal

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Although your episode was brief and spontaneous, the absence of hearing loss, normal audiometry, and a clear MRI rule out Meniere's disease and posterior circulation stroke. The normal imaging suggests the otolith crystals likely migrated, and I recommend performing the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm this diagnosis before treatment.
